## Why This Benchmark Is Included

Retrieval is foundational to search and retrieval-augmented systems.

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Classroom value** | Demonstrates query-document pair construction, batched cross-encoder scoring, and ranking metrics. |
| **Systems behavior** | Variable-length tokenization, encoder attention, batched pair scoring, and ranking. |
| **Benchmark lineage** | Sentence Transformers packages the datasets and evaluator. |
| **Model choice** | The compact MiniLM cross-encoder and exact score are the official upstream evaluator example. |
| **Dataset choice** | NanoBEIR was designed for rapid established retrieval evaluation, and the documented three-dataset subset is only 150 queries. |
| **Quality metric** | The upstream evaluator fixes the retrieval metrics. |
| **Published baseline** | Exact result in the Sentence Transformers evaluator documentation |
| **Alternative rejected** | A custom RAG pipeline would require generator and judge design. |

## Authoritative Sources and Adaptation

| **Field** | **Value** |

| **Authority** | Sentence Transformers and BEIR |
| **Model** | [open source](https://huggingface.co/cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2) |

| **Dataset** | [open source](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sentence-transformers/NanoBEIR-en) |

**Adaptation boundary:** The upstream model, BM25 top-100 candidates, positive-inclusion policy, three documented datasets, and MAP/MRR/nDCG computation are preserved. MLPerf EDU pins the model and Parquet revisions and adds measurement, provenance, and reporting.

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload information-retrieval --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd.json provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload information-retrieval --profile max

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload information-retrieval --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload information-retrieval --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

## Systems Experiment Execution Contract

**Within-run measurement protocol:**

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Primary metric** | inference_and_evaluation_seconds |
| **Scenario** | offline |
| **Timing scope** | one complete cross-encoder scoring and official reranking evaluation for 50 queries and 100 candidate documents in each of three NanoBEIR datasets |
| **Included phases** | tokenization of query-document pairs, batched PyTorch cross-encoder execution, score sorting and MAP, MRR@10, and nDCG@10 computation |
| **Excluded phases** | dataset and model fetching, Parquet loading and sample construction, model construction and one untimed warmup for each scoring batch shape, report and provenance serialization |
| **Device synchronization** | synchronize immediately before and after the measured complete inference-and-evaluation pass |
| **Outer reference runs** | 1 |
| **Outer preconditioning runs** | 0 |
| **Outer inter execution cooldown seconds** | 300 |
| **Repeatability metric** | inference_and_evaluation_seconds |
| **Repeatability limit** | 0.05 |

## Results

To make the metric concrete, one run of this benchmark on Apple M5 Max observed `mean_ndcg_at_10` of 0.6072, taking 17.924 `inference_and_evaluation_seconds`.

That is an illustration, not a target and not a score. It comes from a single machine and your hardware will produce different timing. The number that matters is the one your own run reports.

Run the benchmark and read your own report:

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload information-retrieval --profile max
```

Every run writes an HTML dashboard for reading, JSON for machine use, CSV for spreadsheets, and a `.provd.json` provenance manifest. Those artifacts carry the quality decision, timing distribution, hardware and software fingerprint, asset digests, and model lineage for the run you performed.

See [Reading Results](../../guide/results.qmd) for how to interpret them.
